correctness.rationale: For two exact prime-power blocks X,Y the identity phi*(XY)=(X-1)(Y-1) follows multiplicatively. Writing even=AB with A=2^a and odd=CD, C<D, the orientation AB+1=CD gives C+D=A+B+1 and (D-C)^2-(B-A+1)^2=4(A-1); the reverse orientation gives C+D=A+B-1 and (B-A-1)^2-(D-C)^2=4(A-1). Both even differences factor into positive integers u,v with uv=2^a-1, and solving back produces precisely the three claimed branches with converses verified by products and sums. Filtering exact positive odd prime-power blocks and distinct supports is essential. Under Omega(n),Omega(n+1)<=3 the even block has a<=2; A=2 gives no valid blocks; A=4 gives only (20,21), while (35,36) fails the multiplicity bound. A newly written direct sieve below 300000 recovered [20,35,143,208,2623,5183] and the unique low-Omega point 20. This finite check supports but does not replace the factorization proof.
residual_risks: There is no asserted finiteness or infinitude of unrestricted two-prime-support solutions; prime-power validity is a genuine arithmetic filter.
